root.name: Modern Defense: Lizard Defense, Pirc-Diemer Gambit

overview: White plays 2.h4 and 3.h5 against the Modern Defense, a Pirc-Diemer style pawn thrust. If Black takes 3...Nxh5, White offers the pawn for the h-file with Rxh5 ideas and a quick e4. Black can simply take and consolidate. The Mittenberger Gambit (1.e4 g6 2.d4 Bg7 3.Nc3 d5) is a related Lizard line that the database groups under the same name.

white_ideas.idea: Attack down the h-file with h5 and open lines for Rh1
Build the centre with e4 and develop with Nc3

black_ideas.idea: Take on h5 and consolidate with ...Bg7 and ...d6
Strike in the centre with ...c5 or ...d5

typical_structures.structure: White pawn on h5 versus Black g6 with open h-file

character.notes: A wild pawn-grabbing line where White gambles on a kingside attack.

gambit.notes: 3.h5 Nxh5 gives a pawn that Black can keep.

soundness.notes: Considered unsound; Black is just a pawn up.

structure.notes: White's centre is not fixed and Black has counterplay.

approach.notes: Strong players basically never play it.

level.notes: Dubious so not a repertoire choice.

sublines_that_differ.name: Mittenberger Gambit
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 g6 2. d4 Bg7 3. Nc3 d5
sublines_that_differ.how: Black offers a pawn instead: a separate named line under the same Lizard Defense name.

character.reason: Pawn-grabbing gamble with an h-file attack.

gambit.reason: 3.h5 Nxh5 gives a pawn White cannot easily regain; the related Mittenberger line is a Black pawn offer.

soundness.reason: Black can take the pawn and defend.

structure.reason: White's centre is not fixed and the position is unclear.

approach.reason: Strong players hardly use the Lizard Defense.

plans.reason: White aims at the Black kingside along the h-file.
